title: SpriteGrid just leveled up — browser version is LIVE 🎮
author: TheSpriteWizard
selftext:
You asked, I shipped: SpriteGrid now runs straight in your browser, zero install, zero antivirus drama. Free. Just open it and go.

Drop in any image — AI-generated art, photos, whatever — transform it into clean, proper pixel art using classical algorithms: corner-sampling background removal, median-cut quantization, Bayer dithering, with GameBoy/NES/PICO-8/C64 palettes baked in.

If you've been generating AI art and wishing it actually looked like pixel art instead of mushy upscaled noise, this is for you.

Huge thanks to everyone here who tested the early build and gave honest feedback — seriously shaped where this went. As a gift I am including the prompting I use to get a good sprite.  
  
[https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-grid](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-grid)

\---------------------------------------------------------------

Pipeline:

Prompt:  
Create a single isolated \[SUBJECT\] as a micro-scale fantasy RPG overworld sprite. The sprite should look like a classic 16-bit adventure game asset: low-resolution pixel art, compact full-body silhouette, front-facing or slight 3/4 stance, limited color palette, dark pixel outline, minimal 1–2 step shading, and crisp square pixels with no painterly blur or smooth gradients.

The character should be readable at very small sizes, as if it could be scaled down to a 24x24 or 32x32 RPG map sprite, but generate it large enough for editing. Keep the anatomy simple and practical, not chibi, not overly detailed, and not illustration-like. Prioritize silhouette clarity, strong color blocking, and simple iconic features that identify the subject.

Subject details: \[BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF SUBJECT — species, outfit, weapon/tool, expression, key colors\].

Composition: one full-body sprite only, centered, standing pose, clean edges, no extra characters, no scenery, no dramatic lighting, no complex background. Use a plain solid background so the sprite can be easily separated.

SpriteGrid:   
Upload, increase quantize colors to the max, then remove background. 

Touch up any details you don't like.

Export.

Done.

\--------------------------------------------------

Good luck guys! I hope this helps you guys speed up your work flow like it has mine. 

TheSpriteWizard

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: This appears to be a commercial product (now). See rule #3. Can you clarify? Reading through your page (and please for the love of god make this clear for mods, otherwise we're prone to just nuke posts breaking rule 3) it used to be free, but now is not.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body:
Good morning, Mod! The software is still free. I just moved it to the online version since I was getting so many different messages from devs asking for a more accessible version. 

I placed the original .exe in the five dollar bin since there were so few downloads and if I spend anymore time on it I will have to charge for the time to update and build newer models. I found that doing it in this way keeps the tool free for everyone in case I have to update it and it prevents me from being worried about having to create newer additions.

replies.author: son_o_gong
replies.body: It's true. I was among people who asked to non-windows version (mac user here). The tool looks interesting for me, cos I use a lot outputs from ChatGPT and it doesn't make ready to go pixelart. So a lot manual work needs to be done. And for me this is just a small but accelerator for my workflow.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: That's exactly the workflow I built this for! Really glad the browser version opens it up for Mac users. Let me know how it goes with your ChatGPT outputs — always curious to hear how people are using it in the wild. 🎮

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body:
Quick follow-up addendum: I want to be totally transparent for the mod team — the browser version linked above is and will remain 100% free, no paywall, no signup, nothing. The $5 desktop .exe is a separate optional download for people who want the extra editing tools and offline use; it's not required to use SpriteGrid at all.

Happy to update the page wording if it's unclear — just let me know what would satisfy rule #3 and I'll fix it right away. Appreciate the heads up!

Hello my confused friend,

SpriteGrid doesn’t generate images from prompts, it’s a converter, you bring your own image (from AI, photos, whatever) and it cleans it up into pixel art. Might be a mismatch with what you were expecting? Happy to clarify if you tell me what you tried.

comments.author: forrestwear
comments.body:
i was skeptical at first, but good on you for following through with your word. the universe rewards those who deserve it. good luck on your future endeavors sprite wizard. i doubt many people will buy the 5 dollar version, but if you start your own youtube and build off of this, you'll be on top.

realistically, it's only a matter of time before someone repackages this, makes minor improvements and claims it as their own. but if you can put your ethereal stamp on it, make a video or two on how it works, and frame it in a ''how to make your own sprites for your game in 202x'' and genuinely be a positive flame in this sea of chaos, you will be unstoppable.

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body:
Made me tear up a bit, ngl. Never had such good feedback from something I made. 

Appreciate the honesty, skepticism is fair, I'd rather earn it than ask for it. And yeah, the YouTube idea has been on my mind. A "how to make sprites for your game in 2026" series is basically writing itself at this point. The repackaging risk is real, but the best defense is just being the original voice people find first. Thanks for the push. 🙏
